sync.title: Start on the desktop, carry on on the laptop.
sync.body: When you close the game, Hoard uploads the save; when you open your other PC, it pulls the newer version down. No folder copying, no USB sticks, no overwriting a good save with a stale one.
sync.p1: Automatic: it notices when you stop playing and syncs on its own.
sync.p2: Conflict-aware: if two machines diverge, the most recent wins and the other is backed up locally.
sync.p3: And if anything goes wrong, roll back to any earlier version from the app.
sync.demo_note: The client compares versions with the server and only transfers what changed.
how.title: Three steps. No setup.
how.subtitle: Install the app, sign in once, and forget it's there.
how.s1_body: Download the app for your OS and sign in with Google or an email link. Starts on boot, lives in the tray.
how.s2_body: Hoard finds your games across Steam, Epic, GOG, Proton/Wine prefixes and more, and tracks them on its own. Thousands of titles via the Ludusavi manifest.
how.s3_body: Every time you stop playing, a snapshot is created and synced to your other machines. Roll back to any version from the Library.
features.title: Built like a tool, not a promise
features.subtitle: Everything below ships in the product today, on both tiers.
features.sync.title: Cross-device sync
features.sync.body: Your saves follow you from desktop to laptop. The most recent version wins; the other is backed up locally.
features.versioned.title: Every backup is a snapshot
features.versioned.body: History never expires on any tier. Roll back three weeks, three months, three years.
features.verified.title: SHA-256 on every file
features.verified.body: Content-addressed snapshots, re-hashed on restore. Silent corruption gets caught.
features.detect.title: Picks up your library on its own
features.detect.body: Thousands of titles via the Ludusavi manifest, plus live detection for Steam, Epic, GOG, Proton, Wine, Lutris, Bottles and Heroic.
features.crossplat.title: Windows, macOS, Linux
features.crossplat.body: One desktop app, one account, one set of saves. Proton/Wine prefixes detected as first-class targets.
features.export.title: Yours to leave with
features.export.body: Export every save as the game wrote it — no archive, no proprietary wrapper. Free tier included.
selfhost.title: Same binary, your hardware.
selfhost.body: The server is a single Rust binary under AGPL-3.0. No account, no quotas, no limit but your disk. Runs fine on a Raspberry Pi.

help.title: Help
help.subtitle: Most answers are below. For everything else, write to us — we read everything.
help.no_results: No results. Try a shorter search, or write to us.
help.faq_q1: Is the Free plan actually free?
help.faq_a1: Yes. 1 GB, 3 devices, unlimited saves, sync and full history, no card. Most players never need more.
help.faq_q2: What happens if I cancel Pro?
help.faq_a2: You stay on Pro until the period ends, then drop to Free. Uploads pause if you exceed the Free quota; nothing is deleted.
help.faq_a3: Yes. The server is a single Rust binary, AGPL-3.0. The repo README covers Docker and bare-metal.
help.faq_a4: Snapshots are encrypted at rest in Cloudflare R2. End-to-end encryption (with a key we never see) is on the roadmap.
help.faq_a5: EU (Frankfurt) — Postgres and object storage. We don't replicate outside the EU.
help.faq_q6: Is there a size limit per save?
help.faq_a6: 200 MB per save on Free, 2 GB on Pro. Modern games rarely exceed 200 MB of save data; if yours do, Pro covers them.
help.faq_a7: Rolling 15-minute window: 1 GB on Free, 5 GB on Pro. Plenty for normal sync. If you hit it, the app waits and resumes on its own.
help.contact_body: Write to support@hoard.services or open a GitHub issue. We read everything, on any plan.
